requirements.description: The system MUST create a student record capturing roll number, first name, last name, father's or guardian's name, gender, date of birth, primary mobile number, alternate mobile number, course and year of admission.
acceptance_criteria: Given a complete and valid set of the ten field values, when the operator submits the create form, then exactly one student record is persisted and is retrievable by its roll number.
Given a successful create, when the operation returns, then the operator receives explicit confirmation naming the roll number that was created.

requirements.description: The system MUST reject a create or amend request in which any mandatory field is absent, rather than relying on a runtime exception to enforce presence.
acceptance_criteria: Given the gender, course or year-of-admission selection is empty, when the operator submits, then the system reports which specific field is missing and persists nothing.
Given a mandatory text field is empty or whitespace, when the operator submits, then the system reports that field by name and persists nothing.
Given any rejected submission, when the error is reported, then no unhandled exception is raised and no raw provider message is shown.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy made three dropdowns mandatory only by accident: an unselected combo threw NullReferenceException into a catch-all handler and was reported to the user as a database error. Presence is prescribed explicitly and attributed to the offending field.

requirements.description: The system MUST validate every field against an explicit, declared rule before persisting it, covering presence, maximum length, and format for the two mobile-number fields and the roll number.
acceptance_criteria: Given a mobile number that is not a valid telephone number for the configured locale, when the operator submits, then the system rejects it and names the field.

Given input longer than the declared maximum length for a field, when the operator types, then the field prevents further entry; and when a longer value arrives by any other route, then the system rejects it rather than truncating silently.
Given a valid submission, when it is persisted, then no value has been silently altered or truncated.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy performed no validation on any free-text field and set no MaxLength on any text box, so an all-empty-string record was persistable. Validation is a NEW requirement here, not a port.

requirements.description: The system MUST reject a create request whose roll number already identifies an existing student record, reporting the collision to the operator.
acceptance_criteria: Given a roll number that already exists, when the operator submits a create, then the system rejects the request, states that the roll number is already in use, and persists nothing.
Given two concurrent creates with the same roll number, when both are submitted, then exactly one succeeds and the other is rejected with the collision message.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy performed no duplicate check on the create path and relied on an index whose existence two Discovery passes disputed; see synthesis contradiction CON-001.

requirements.description: The system MUST retrieve exactly one student record by roll number for amendment, and MUST report explicitly when no record matches rather than presenting an empty form.
acceptance_criteria: Given a roll number that exists, when the operator opens the record for amendment, then every stored field is populated in the form.
Given a roll number that does not exist, when the operator opens it for amendment, then the system states that no such record exists and does not present an editable blank form.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy read the result set with an If-without-Else, so a missing record silently yielded a blank edit form whose subsequent save reported success while updating zero rows.

requirements.description: The system MUST amend the mutable fields of exactly one student record identified by roll number, and MUST NOT modify any other record.
acceptance_criteria: Given a roll number identifying one record, when the operator saves an amendment, then exactly one record is modified and the system confirms the count.
Given an amendment that matches zero records, when it is executed, then the system reports that nothing was changed rather than reporting success.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy discarded the affected-row count from every mutation, so a zero-row update reported 'Record updated successfully'. The target must surface the count.

requirements.description: The system MUST treat the roll number as immutable once a record exists; it MUST NOT be editable through the amend path.
acceptance_criteria: Given a record open for amendment, when the operator attempts to change the roll number, then the field is not editable and the value is unchanged on save.

requirements.description: The system MUST permit amendment of a record whose stored categorical value falls outside the currently offered value set, and MUST NOT silently discard that value.
acceptance_criteria: Given a record whose stored course or gender is not in the current offered set, when the operator opens it for amendment, then the system displays the stored value and states that it is outside the current set.
Given such a record, when the operator saves without touching that field, then the stored value is preserved unchanged.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy assigned the stored value to a dropdown's selected item; an unlisted value failed silently and left the control blank, so saving overwrote the real value and the record became permanently un-editable.

requirements.description: The system MUST list student records in a stable, explicitly declared order, and MUST page or bound the result set rather than returning the whole table.
acceptance_criteria: Given more records than one page holds, when the operator opens the list, then a bounded page is returned with a deterministic order and a means of reaching subsequent pages.
Given the same data and the same request, when the list is requested twice, then the order is identical.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy bound SELECT * with no ORDER BY and no paging straight to a grid, so order was engine-defined and the whole table was read on every refresh.

requirements.description: The system MUST search student records using parameterized queries only; it MUST NOT construct any query by concatenating operator input.
acceptance_criteria: Given a search term containing SQL metacharacters including a single quote, when the search executes, then the term is treated as data, results are correct, and no error occurs.
Given any search, when the query is issued, then every operator-supplied value is bound as a parameter.
Given a surname containing an apostrophe, when it is searched, then the matching record is returned and the process does not terminate.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy concatenated the search box verbatim into an equality clause and a LIKE clause — the application's only attacker-controlled unparameterized statement and a live data-disclosure path. It is also an availability defect: a legitimate apostrophe crashed the process.

requirements.description: The system SHOULD offer search and filtering across the fields an operator needs to find a record, with the semantics of each search field declared, and SHOULD NOT silently mix exact and partial matching in one undifferentiated input.
acceptance_criteria: Given a search by roll number, when it executes, then the declared matching semantics for that field are applied and are documented in the interface.
Given a search by name, when it executes, then partial matching is applied as declared.
Given a request to filter by course or year of admission, when it is made, then the system supports it.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy applied exact equality to roll number and partial LIKE to first name from a single box, ignored the other seven stored fields, and offered no filter by course or year even though those are the dashboard's primary reporting axes.

requirements.description: The system MUST require explicit confirmation before removing a student record, and MUST state in the confirmation which record will be removed.
acceptance_criteria: Given a record selected for removal, when the operator initiates it, then a confirmation naming the roll number is presented and nothing is removed until it is accepted.
Given the confirmation is declined, when control returns, then no record has been modified or removed.

requirements.description: The system MUST remove exactly the one student record identified for removal, and MUST NOT remove any other record.
acceptance_criteria: Given a roll number identifying one record, when removal executes, then exactly one record is affected and the count is reported.
Given a removal that would affect more than one record, when it is attempted, then the system refuses and reports the ambiguity.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy keyed update and delete on a roll number with no enforced uniqueness, so duplicates would cause every matching row to be rewritten or removed while success was reported.

requirements.description: The system MUST implement removal as a reversible, audited state change that retains the record and its history, rather than as an immediate physical deletion.
acceptance_criteria: Given a record is removed, when the store is inspected, then the record is retained in a removed state with the actor, the timestamp and the prior values recorded.
Given a removed record, when an authorized operator requests its restoration, then the record is restored with its field values intact.
Given a removed record, when the standard list or search is used, then it does not appear.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy deletion was physical, immediate and unrecoverable with no audit, archive or retention, while forensics nonetheless recovered six deleted rows from page slack — so the data was neither recoverable by the operator nor actually destroyed. Subject to the retention ruling in synthesis open question OQ-009.

requirements.description: The system SHOULD allow an authorized operator to act on more than one selected record where the operation is well defined, and MUST apply the same confirmation and audit rules to each.
acceptance_criteria: Given several records are selected, when a bulk operation is applied, then each record is processed under the same validation, confirmation and audit rules as a single-record operation.
Given a bulk operation in which one record fails, when it completes, then the outcome per record is reported and no partial inconsistent state is left behind.

requirements.description: The system MUST clear every field of the record-entry form after a successful create, including all selection fields, so that no value carries over into the next entry.
acceptance_criteria: Given a successful create, when the form resets, then every text field is empty and every selection field is returned to its unselected state.

Given a second consecutive create, when the operator submits without touching a selection field, then the system rejects it for a missing mandatory field rather than silently reusing the previous record's value.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy reset routine could not clear a drop-down-list combo by assigning its text property, so the second and subsequent inserts silently inherited the previous record's gender, course and year.

requirements.description: The system MUST record the student's date of birth as a date value, independent of the display culture of any client, and MUST reject an implausible date.
acceptance_criteria: Given a date of birth entered on a client in one locale, when it is read on a client in a different locale, then the same calendar date is presented.
Given a date of birth in the future, or one implying an implausible age at admission, when the operator submits, then the system rejects it and states the rule applied.
Given a stored date of birth, when it is round-tripped through amendment without being changed, then the stored value is byte-for-byte unchanged.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy wrote the date from a culture-formatted display string and read it back with a culture-free parse under OptionStrict Off, making day/month transposition possible across workstation locales. No plausibility check existed; the two live records carry a 2009 date of birth against a 2019 admission year.

requirements.description: The system MUST derive every academic-year statistic from the current date at the time the statistic is computed, and MUST NOT use a compiled-in year constant.
acceptance_criteria: Given the system clock reads a given year, when the statistics are computed, then every academic-year bucket is derived from that year.
Given the clock advances across a year boundary, when the statistics are next computed, then the buckets shift accordingly with no code change and no redeployment.
Given a computed statistic, when it is presented, then the as-at date used to compute it is shown alongside it.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy derived all five academic-year statistics by subtraction from a hardcoded constant 2023 and never read the clock, so every cohort has been mislabelled since 1 January 2024. The error was silent: no exception, no reconciling total, and changing the workstation clock had no effect. Intended definition subject to synthesis open question OQ-008.

requirements.description: The system MUST count every stored record in exactly one bucket of each reported statistical breakdown, and MUST present a reconciling total against which each breakdown can be checked.
acceptance_criteria: Given records holding every value of the gender set including values outside the primary ones, when the gender breakdown is computed, then the buckets sum to the reported total record count.
Given a record whose categorical value is absent, empty or outside the declared set, when the breakdown is computed, then it is counted in an explicit residual bucket rather than omitted.
Given any presented breakdown, when it is displayed, then the reconciling total is displayed with it.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy counted only two of the three storable gender values and reported no grand total, so any record recorded as the third value was invisible in every statistic and the undercount was undetectable from the screen. The same defect applies to admissions before the earliest recognised cohort.

requirements.description: The system MUST derive the set of reported course and academic-year breakdowns from the stored reference data, and MUST NOT require a code or query change to report on a newly added course or intake year.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new course is added to the reference data, when the statistics are computed, then a breakdown for that course appears with no code change.
Given a new intake year is added, when the statistics are computed, then a bucket for it appears with no code change.
Given a course with no records, when the breakdown is computed, then it is reported as zero rather than omitted.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy hardcoded each course as its own COUNT query with no GROUP BY, restating the course taxonomy in at least eight places, so adding a course required editing two interface definition files and the dashboard query set.

requirements.description: The system MUST compare academic-year values arithmetically against a numeric or date-typed stored value, and MUST NOT match them as text.
acceptance_criteria: Given an academic-year bucket covering a range, when it is computed, then records are selected by numeric comparison.
Given a stored admission year, when it is sorted or range-queried, then the ordering is numeric and not lexical.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy stored the admission year as text and matched it by concatenating a literal into the query, so comparison was lexical rather than arithmetic. This was also the application's second site of query concatenation, non-injectable only because the interpolated value was an integer.

requirements.description: The system SHOULD allow a statistic to be scoped, and MUST state the scope of every statistic it presents.
acceptance_criteria: Given a presented statistic, when it is displayed, then the population it covers is stated.
Given a request for a statistic over a subset of the population, when the system supports that scope, then the scope is applied and restated in the output.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy statistics were whole-table and all-time with no status, enrolment or date scope, and the absence of scope was nowhere stated.

requirements.description: The system MUST distinguish a statistic of zero from a statistic that could not be computed, and MUST NOT present an unavailable value as a zero.
acceptance_criteria: Given the statistics cannot be computed, when the view is presented, then each affected statistic is shown as unavailable with the reason, and not as zero.
Given a genuine count of zero, when it is presented, then it is shown as zero and is visually distinguishable from unavailable.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy statistics defaulted to the literal zero in non-editable labels and the load path was wholly unguarded, so any query failure left a screen of plausible zeros indistinguishable from a real empty population.

requirements.description: The system MUST refresh every presented statistic after any operation that changes the underlying records, by a single consistent mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: Given a record is created, amended or removed, when the operation succeeds, then every presented statistic reflects the change without further operator action.
Given any of the three mutation paths, when it completes, then the refresh behaviour is identical.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy had three mutation paths with three mutually inconsistent refresh behaviours and omitted the refresh entirely after removal, so the statistics silently diverged from the records.

requirements.description: The system MUST reflect the result of every completed operation in the interface the operator is actually looking at.
acceptance_criteria: Given a record is created, when the operation succeeds, then the list and the statistics visible to that operator show the new record without further action.
Given any mutation, when the refresh executes, then it targets the interface in use and no update is applied to a surface the operator cannot see.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy refreshed siblings through language default-instance properties that resolved to different objects than the displayed ones, so after a successful create the application updated two off-screen forms while the visible list and statistics stayed stale. The target language has no equivalent mechanism, so the navigation and refresh contract must be re-specified rather than translated.

requirements.description: The system MUST allow the operator to move between the statistics view, the record list and the record-entry and amendment forms, and MUST release the resources of a view that is no longer in use.
acceptance_criteria: Given the operator navigates away from a view and back, when the view is presented again, then it reflects current data and no duplicated handling of any event occurs.
Given repeated navigation between all views, when it is exercised, then the number of retained view instances and event subscriptions does not grow.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy navigation reparented child forms into a single host panel and only hid them, never releasing them; it is recorded as the single highest-complexity behaviour in the application and accumulated event subscriptions on each reuse.

requirements.description: The system SHOULD allow the operator to close the application from the standard window control as well as from an in-application control, and MUST warn before discarding unsaved entry.
acceptance_criteria: Given unsaved data in an entry form, when the operator attempts to close the application, then a warning is presented and closing is cancellable.
Given no unsaved data, when the operator closes the application, then it closes without further prompting.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy suppressed the window control box entirely, making a single in-application button the only way to exit, with no unsaved-data prompt at any point.

requirements.description: The system MUST authenticate every operator before granting access to any student record data or any statistic.
acceptance_criteria: Given an unauthenticated request for any record or statistic, when it is made, then it is refused and no data is returned.
Given a successful authentication, when the session is established, then the operator's identity is available to every subsequent operation for authorization and audit.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy had no authentication of any kind: no login form, no user concept, no roles, no permission check and no audit column, so anyone who launched the executable had unrestricted create, read, update and delete over all personal data. Every requirement in this module is a new prescription correcting a security violation.

requirements.description: The system MUST authorize each operation against the authenticated operator's permissions, and MUST refuse an operation the operator is not permitted to perform.
acceptance_criteria: Given an operator without permission to remove records, when a removal is attempted, then it is refused, nothing is changed, and the refusal is audited.
Given an operator with read-only permission, when any mutation is attempted, then it is refused and nothing is changed.
requirements.anomaly_details: The closest thing to an access check in the legacy system was a test that a grid row had been selected. Permission semantics and the role set are subject to synthesis open question OQ-011, which asks whether more than one operator role exists.

requirements.description: The system MUST record an audit entry for every create, amend and remove operation, capturing the acting operator, the timestamp, the record affected and the values before and after.
acceptance_criteria: Given any successful mutation, when the audit store is inspected, then an entry exists naming the operator, the time, the record and the prior and new values.
Given a refused or failed mutation, when the audit store is inspected, then the attempt is recorded with its outcome.
Given an audit entry, when any operator attempts to alter or remove it, then the attempt is refused.
requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy schema carried no audit, provenance, soft-delete or row-version column of any kind, and with no authentication there was no actor to attribute a change to. No change to any record in the legacy system can be reconstructed, and that history is already unrecoverable.

requirements.description: The system MUST execute each unit of work in an explicit transaction that commits as a whole or not at all.
acceptance_criteria: Given a multi-statement unit of work, when any statement fails, then no part of the unit is persisted.
Given a unit of work that commits, when it returns, then every change in it is durable.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy used no transaction anywhere: each mutation was a single autocommitted statement with no atomicity beyond one statement.

requirements.description: The system MUST detect a conflicting concurrent change to a student record and MUST refuse the later write rather than overwriting silently.
acceptance_criteria: Given two operators load the same record and both save, when the second save is attempted, then it is refused with a statement that the record changed, and the first operator's change is intact.
Given a refused write, when the operator re-reads the record, then current values are presented and the operation can be retried.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy permitted concurrent instances against one file database with last-write-wins, no row version and no conflict detection of any kind.

requirements.description: The system MUST acquire a database connection per unit of work and MUST release it deterministically when that unit of work ends, including on failure.
acceptance_criteria: Given a unit of work completes or fails, when it returns, then its connection has been released and the pool shows no leak.
Given one operation fails mid-way, when a subsequent independent operation runs, then it succeeds and is unaffected by the earlier failure.
Given sustained use across every operation type, when connection usage is measured, then it remains bounded.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy held one process-wide connection opened lazily and never disposed, with no using block anywhere; a single unclosed reader blocked every other operation.

requirements.description: The system MUST ensure that no component can render the data layer unusable for other components.
acceptance_criteria: Given any operation including removal completes, when any other operation is invoked afterwards, then it succeeds.
Given a connection in a failed state, when the data layer is next used, then it recovers or fails with a clear diagnostic rather than executing against an unusable connection.
requirements.anomaly_details: In the legacy system the removal path closed the shared global connection and no reopen was paired with it, so a subsequent statistics refresh threw an unhandled exception. The connection helper also tested only for the closed state, so a broken or connecting state fell through and every caller proceeded against it.

requirements.description: The system MUST obtain its database location and credentials from external configuration, and MUST NOT embed them in compiled code.
acceptance_criteria: Given a deployment to a new environment, when configuration alone is changed, then the system connects to that environment's database with no recompilation.
Given the configured database is unreachable, when the system starts, then it reports the failure with the configured target identified, and does not expose any credential.
Given the source tree is inspected, when it is searched, then no database path or credential literal is present.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy pinned an absolute path on the original author's drive as the only database binding, declared no connection-string configuration section and left its settings store empty, so a clean checkout could not connect to the database shipped beside it.

requirements.description: The system MUST declare an enforced unique identifier for a student record in the database schema itself, not in application code alone.
acceptance_criteria: Given an attempt to persist two records with the same identifier, when it reaches the database, then the database rejects it irrespective of the application path used.
Given an attempt to persist an empty identifier, when it reaches the database, then it is rejected.
Given records are listed in identifier order, when the order is inspected, then it is the declared order and not an accident of text collation.
requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy key was a text column admitting the empty string, ordering lexically so that a roll number of ten sorted before two, with no uniqueness enforced in code. Two Discovery passes disputed whether any key index existed at all; see synthesis contradiction CON-001 and open question OQ-003.

requirements.description: The system MUST store each field in a data type that can represent every value the interface accepts, and MUST declare the type, nullability and length of every column explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid telephone number of the maximum length the locale permits, when it is persisted and read back, then the value is unchanged.
Given each column in the target schema, when the schema is inspected, then its type, nullability and maximum length are declared explicitly.
Given a value that exceeds a declared column length, when it is submitted, then it is rejected before reaching the database rather than truncated or overflowed.
requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy mobile-number columns were a four-byte integer type that cannot hold a ten-digit number at all, while the interface accepted one without complaint. Note that the legacy types themselves are contested — see synthesis contradiction CON-002 — so the target schema MUST NOT be generated until open question OQ-003 is closed.

requirements.description: The system MUST hold the course, gender and academic-year reference sets as stored reference data with a single system of record, and MUST NOT restate them in interface or query code.
acceptance_criteria: Given a reference set is amended in its system of record, when any interface or statistic that uses it is next used, then the amendment is reflected with no code change.
Given the source tree is searched, when reference values are sought, then no literal member of any reference set appears in interface or query code.
Given a new intake year is required, when it is added to the reference data, then it becomes selectable with no code change.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy restated the academic-year set in four places and the course set in at least eight, enforced all three sets only in the interface and never in the database, and the academic-year list expired at 2023 so no later intake could be recorded at all. Cardinality and intent are subject to synthesis open question OQ-013.

requirements.description: The system MUST migrate the existing student records into the target schema with no silent alteration of any value, and MUST reconcile the migrated record count and field values against the source.
acceptance_criteria: Given the legacy store, when migration completes, then the migrated record count equals the verified source record count and the reconciliation is recorded.
Given each migrated record, when its fields are compared to the source, then every value is equal under the declared type mapping, with any date conversion explicitly recorded.
Given duplicate or empty identifiers in the source, when migration runs, then they are reported and resolved before load rather than carried forward.
requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy store holds a superseded column layout alongside the live one, carries deleted rows recoverable from page slack, and has no authoritative row count agreed between Discovery passes — see synthesis contradictions CON-003 and CON-012. Migration must establish the baseline rather than assume it.

requirements.description: The system MUST report a failed operation to the operator in terms of the business action attempted, and MUST NOT surface raw provider or exception text.
acceptance_criteria: Given any failure, when it is reported to the operator, then the message describes the action and the corrective step and contains no provider or stack detail.
Given any failure, when it is logged, then the technical detail is recorded in the log with a correlation reference shown to the operator.
Given a validation failure, when it is reported, then it names the specific field at fault.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy wrapped each mutation in a catch-all that displayed the raw provider exception text in a message box, with no logging and no field attribution, so a missing dropdown selection was reported to the operator as a database error.

requirements.description: The system MUST remain available and MUST NOT terminate when a data operation fails.
acceptance_criteria: Given a data operation fails during record retrieval, when the failure is handled, then the system reports it and remains usable.
Given any single failure, when it has been reported, then the operator can retry or navigate elsewhere without restarting.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy performed unguarded database input and output inside a form constructor, so every load failure terminated the application.

requirements.description: The system MUST determine the fields presented in the record list from an explicit declared contract, and MUST NOT derive them from the physical schema at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Given the record list, when it is presented, then its fields and their order match the declared contract.
Given a physical column is renamed in the store, when the list is presented, then either it is unaffected or the build fails; it MUST NOT change the operator-visible contract silently.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy bound the grid with automatic column generation over SELECT *, so the physical schema defined the operator-visible contract, column headers were raw database field names, and cell lookups by name failed at runtime rather than at build time.

requirements.description: The system SHOULD retain an active search filter across a refresh, or MUST state that the filter has been cleared.
acceptance_criteria: Given an active filter, when a refresh is triggered by any path, then the filter is still applied or its removal is stated to the operator.
requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy discarded an active filter silently on every refresh path, and an empty search was the only way to clear a filter.

requirements.description: The system MUST present only rows that correspond to stored records in the record list, and MUST NOT present a placeholder row that can be selected for an operation.
acceptance_criteria: Given the record list, when it is inspected, then every row corresponds to a stored record.
Given no record is selected, when an operation requiring a selection is invoked, then the system states that a selection is required and does not fail.
requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy grid was read-only yet retained its default add-row affordance, so an empty phantom row was selectable and its null identifier cell crashed both the amend and the remove paths.

requirements.description: The system SHOULD provide the reporting output its reporting affordance offers, generated from current data, and MUST NOT present an external document as a system report.
acceptance_criteria: Given the operator requests a report, when it is produced, then it is generated from current system data and identifies the data and the as-at time.
Given no network connectivity, when a report is requested, then it is still produced.
requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy report control generated nothing: it launched the operator's browser at a hardcoded public third-party URL for the author's project document, which was the application's only outbound network call and left any genuine reporting requirement unimplemented. Confirmed as a requirements gap rather than an integration to migrate.
